description: A rising zigzag producing two swing lows and two swing highs, so each kind gets a predecessor and the HH / HL labels are actually assigned.
labelling_rationale: The three existing structure datasets all confirm at most one swing, so §3.3 has never been exercised: a first swing has no same-kind predecessor and is SEED, which this engine represents by emitting no classification event. This series confirms four internal swings under the §3.1 k_int = 2 rule. Lows are [103,101,99,101,103,108,106,104,106,108,110,113,111,109,107]: index 2 at 99 has nothing lower in its window and two strictly higher lows to its right, and index 7 at 104 likewise sits below 108 and 106 on its left with 106 and 108 to its right. Highs are [105,103,101,103,105,110,108,106,108,110,112,115,113,111,109]: index 5 at 110 is unexceeded in its window with 108 and 106 strictly lower to its right, and index 11 at 115 has 113 and 111 strictly lower to its right. Every other evaluable index is dominated by one of these four. §3.3 then labels each swing against its immediate same-kind predecessor: the low at index 7 is 104 against the earlier 99, and 104 > 99 gives HL; the high at index 11 is 115 against the earlier 110, and 115 > 110 gives HH. The first low and the first high have no same-kind predecessor and so carry SEED, which as of SLS v1.0.2 is emitted as a classification event rather than skipped — giving four classification events in total: SEED for the low at index 2, SEED for the high at index 5, then HL and HH. SEED asserts no direction and is excluded from every directional set, so adding it changes the record without changing any downstream judgement. Indices above are scenario-relative; the 285 declared filler candles (§1.9 warm-up) shift them by 285 in the expected output, so the low at scenario index 2 is absolute index 287. External strength: k_ext = 5 needs five candles either side. Every high candidate is dominated inside its eleven-candle window — the 110 at scenario index 5 is beaten by the 112 at index 10, and the 110 at index 9 by the 115 at index 11 — so no external swing HIGH confirms. One external swing LOW does: the 99 at scenario index 2 (absolute 287) now has a full left window of declared history at 103 and scenario lows of 103 and 101, nothing lower anywhere in the window, and five strictly higher lows to its right (101, 103, 108, 106, 104). Note that this detection is ONLY reachable with history — the original fifteen-candle version of this dataset could not judge that candle at all, and under-reported as a result. Being the first external swing of its kind it carries SEED, which asserts no direction, so §3.4 still has no HH/HL pair on external structure and the trend stays RANGING; the BOS replay reads the same RANGING state and emits nothing. That separation is the point of the case: internal structure can be unambiguously bullish while the external trend is honestly still unknown, and §3.2's rule of authority forbids the former from overriding the latter. Corrected 2026-08-23: the swing at index 287 was expected twice, once as SWING_EXTERNAL_LOW and once as SWING_INTERNAL_LOW. §3.1 allows one -- "every external swing is by construction also an internal swing; it is stored once with strength = external" -- so the internal copy was never doctrine, and the label carried the engine's duplicate rather than the spec's rule. Its five classification events are untouched: §3.3 labels per strength class and the two classes can legitimately disagree about one pivot, so those are two facts rather than one fact twice.
